I will still start from what I know from the last few years: on my 12 mu, grain has to stay steady first, because wheat and maize pay the bills and keep risk down. I have well irrigation, so I will lean on that and not farm too conservatively. I have high school-level thinking, so I do not just copy one fixed rate. I look at what each crop removes, what the soil can hold, and what gives me a safe yield on my land in Quzhou. For wheat-maize, I will keep 8 mu in the full double-crop cycle because that is the backbone. I will leave 2 mu for chili and 2 mu for cotton to keep some cash-crop income, but I will not expand them too much because they need more labor and more pesticide, and my household only has 2 people. On fertilizer, I would rather spend a bit more than cut too hard and lose yield, especially on wheat, maize, and chili. On wheat I will push for stable ears and grain weight, so nitrogen will not be low, but I will still keep phosphorus and potassium in balance. On maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed and no-tillage sowing to save time and catch moisture. On chili, I will feed more potassium because fruit set and color depend on it, and I will irrigate more often because once chili dries too hard, yield drops fast. On cotton, I will not chase extreme input, but I will still keep enough fertilizer and water for boll setting. I will watch costs across the whole farm, but grain security comes first, cash crops second.
